unlisted_practices: Professional psychotherapy organisations and training programmes should unite to alert psychotherapists and society that AI poses great dangers and must be much better regulated.
Advocate strongly for AI transparency, privacy protections and safety surveillance for psychotherapy chatbots.
Train or retrain human therapists to treat patients unsuitable for AI therapy, such as those with severe, complex or uncommon problems, and to work in settings too novel or complex for chatbots.
Refocus psychotherapy training programmes away from milder mental disorders and toward techniques AI cannot do, such as family and group therapy.
Train human therapists in AI quality control, correcting AI errors, and leading and guiding the training of teams of AI agents.

screen.reason: Editorial discussing the risks, benefits, and governance needs of AI chatbots in psychotherapy, along with recommendations on how therapists must adapt.
